title: Stop Chromium Google OAuth workaround that causes SIGTRAP crashes
head: 617efa7db5c3
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Open PR #12244 and this PR make the same command do opposite things
leads.consequence: They are diverged, not stacked. #12244 always appends OAuth switches from overrideable credentials (including re-runs), whereas #11907 removes those switches and installs Chrome; the two new shell tests assert contradictory outcomes. The three-way merged command has conflict markers, so merging either after the other requires choosing one policy and revising the other's fixtures/docs. #12244's separate security-floor migration is independent and need not be discarded.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F6 (#12244 opposite direction, conflict)

leads.summary: An OAuth-only flags file causes both removal paths to exit before replacing it
leads.consequence: grep -vE emits zero lines and exits 1. Under installer's set -e and omarchy-migrate's bash -euo pipefail this aborts before mv; the OAuth flags remain, installer never calls the Chrome installer, and migration never stamps a marker, blocking subsequent pending migrations until repaired. On retry the same failure repeats. The new test always retains unrelated flags, so it misses this case.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1 (OAuth-only file, set -e); published

leads.summary: Cleanup misses valid Chromium launcher flags written with whitespace or combined on one line
leads.consequence: Both regexes require the option at column one. The Arch Chromium launcher v8 uses g_shell_parse_argv per line, accepting leading whitespace, several switches on one line, and shell-quoted arguments. Those usable OAuth switches survive upgrade and running the installer, so the purportedly unsafe option is still supplied to Chromium. The menu's unanchored disabled check, however, continues offering the cleanup action after Chrome is present, and repeated clicks cannot resolve it.
leads.triage: leading-whitespace part corroborates Opus F3 (published in Details); 'combined on one line' variant not separately published (Opus found lines starting with the flag are stripped; mid-line variants are hand-edited edge cases)

leads.summary: Related PR #10446 would restore a Chromium-only visibility guard on the new Chrome installer entry
leads.consequence: #10446 intentionally removes Chromium from fresh installs, then rewrites this exact row to `when:omarchy-cmd-present chromium` and labels it Chromium Account; its test requires that expression. If that side of the conflict is selected after #11907, users without Chromium cannot access the Google Account (Chrome) service installer, even if Chrome is missing, while the action still strips flags and installs Chrome. Conversely choosing #11907's row makes #10446's menu test fail. The three-way merge of both row and test has conflict markers, and both PRs' menu tests need a shared resolved expectation.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (sol/10446.diff lines 215-216, 661-663: #10446 rewrites the same row's when and menu-test assertion); published in Details; Opus self-check also confirmed

leads.summary: Migration and installer ignore the active flags file when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set
leads.consequence: Arch's pinned launcher prefers `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/chromium-flags.conf` when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set. The PR always edits `$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf` instead. Upgraded users whose active config is in the XDG directory keep the OAuth switches there; the migration exits 0 and is stamped as done. The menu guards also inspect the wrong location and may hide the only repair option when Chrome is installed. Users with default HOME/.config are unaffected.
leads.triage: dropped: XDG_CONFIG_HOME location; the old installer, refresh-config and menu all use ~/.config/chromium-flags.conf, so this is a repo-wide convention, not introduced here

leads.summary: Rewriting a symlinked flags file silently detaches the user's dotfile source
leads.consequence: `[[ -f symlink ]]` succeeds and `mv temp destination` replaces the symlink itself with a plain file; the dotfile manager's target retains the old OAuth flags. Chromium sees the temporary cleaned file until the symlink is restored on a future sync, when the OAuth switches return. No backup or warning preserves the original link. Both installer and migration use this pattern.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4 (symlink/mode); published in Details

leads.summary: Menu offers a no-op cleanup action when a comment merely mentions an OAuth flag
leads.consequence: The disabled expression searches for an OAuth substring anywhere, but the installer strips only a line beginning with the switch. With Chrome installed and `# --oauth2-client-id=example` in the flags file, the row remains clickable forever even though Chromium skips that comment and running the action changes nothing. Align the menu predicate to the same meaningful flags as the remover and Chromium launcher.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 (commented line keeps row selectable); published in Details

leads.summary: Four open browser PRs conflict with the refresh rewrite and require preserving their hooks
leads.consequence: #13189 adds an NVIDIA video-decode fixer and relies on CONFIG_FILE that this PR deletes; #13762 adds a legacy-radeon fixer, #10884 a theme-sync installer, and #13481 an opt-in webapp-links enabler. Each three-way merge against its own common base has conflict markers. A resolution retaining only this PR's short refresh script discards their new hooks. A resolution retaining the old OAuth tail can instead call this PR's repurposed installer on refresh when the prior flags were present; after refresh resets them, the call installs Chrome from AUR without the user choosing the service action. #13189's video-decode helper call survives outside the conflict markers: if its source line is dropped it becomes command-not-found, and if the helper is sourced but CONFIG_FILE is dropped it silently skips the empty target. None is stacked.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F6 (four refresh-chromium conflicts, #13189 CONFIG_FILE); published in Details

leads.summary: New installer test ignores the program exit status and has no migration fixture
leads.consequence: The test lacks set -e, so both `output=$(omarchy-install-chromium-google-account)` assignments can return nonzero yet execution proceeds; a plausible script that successfully strips flags and logs browser install but returns nonzero makes both cases print pass even though the menu terminal reports failure. It never invokes migrations/1789450436.sh, so the migration's OAuth-only failure also passes the stated test plan. Assert the installer status explicitly and add a direct migration fixture with only the OAuth lines.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator reading (test/shell runs each file with bash, base-test.sh has no errexit, no status check at test lines 46/64); published as part of the Optional test note

leads.summary: The asserted OAuth-switch-to-SIGTRAP causal link is not established by the source examined
leads.consequence: Arch's actual Chromium 151 packaging deliberately patches the Google API key cache to read these switches, and Chromium's switch handler reads the values without an inherent trap at the supplied pair. This does not exclude a crash later in the sign-in/search flow, but source inspection alone cannot prove the PR's claim that the reported Chromium 136+/151 Google Search and sign-in crashes are caused by this workaround. Avoid categorical crash claims until an A/B reproducer at the shipped build records the failing stack and shows only toggling these flags changes it; otherwise the migration may not cure the reported crash.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2 (premise not isolated); published in Details as wording suggestion

limits: No Chromium GUI process or Google account was launched; H10 remains explicitly a hypothesis requiring an isolated A/B browser reproducer, not a proven causal defect.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A flags file that holds only the two OAuth lines makes the new migration fail, stopping the migration queue and (by source reading) `omarchy update` each run.

### OAuth-only flags file stops the migration and the installer

`grep -vE ... >"$tmp"` selects no lines and exits 1, and `set -e` (the installer's `set -euo pipefail`, and `omarchy-migrate`'s `bash -euo pipefail`) stops the script before `mv`, with no error message. **Impact:** the migration stays pending and blocks every later migration; the installer exits before installing Chrome and the menu row stays selectable. The old installer appended to any existing file, so this arises when the file held nothing else.

**Suggested change:** replace the `mktemp`/`grep -v`/`mv` lines with `sed -i --follow-symlinks -E '/^--oauth2-client-(id|secret)=/d'` on `"$file"` (installer) and `"$CONF"` (migration).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 617efa7)</summary>

Append one block at a time to `test/shell.d/chromium-google-account-test.sh` (the PR's own test, which provides `$ROOT`, `$HOME`, the stubs and `fail`/`pass`), then run `bash test/shell.d/chromium-google-account-test.sh`.

Block 1, the migration:

```bash
# The old installer appended to whatever flags file existed, so a file can hold
# nothing but the two workaround lines. omarchy-migrate runs each migration
# with `bash -euo pipefail`, as here.
printf '%s\n' '--oauth2-client-id=77185425430.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
  '--oauth2-client-secret=OTJgUOQcT7lO7GsGZq2G4IlT' >"$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf"
output=$(bash -euo pipefail "$ROOT/migrations/1789450436.sh" 2>&1) ||
  fail "migration strips a flags file that holds only the workaround" "exit $?: $output"
grep -qE -- '^--oauth2-client-(id|secret)=' "$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf" &&
  fail "migration strips a flags file that holds only the workaround" "$(cat "$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf")"
pass "migration strips a flags file that holds only the workaround"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit 1):

```text
ok - installer removes oauth2 workaround flags and installs Chrome when missing
ok - installer skips Chrome when it is already present
exit 1: Remove Chromium Google OAuth workaround that causes SIGTRAP crashes
not ok - migration strips a flags file that holds only the workaround
```

Block 2, the installer:

```bash
rm -f "$HOME/actions.log"
export STUB_GOOGLE_CHROME_PRESENT=0
printf '%s\n' '--oauth2-client-id=77185425430.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
  '--oauth2-client-secret=OTJgUOQcT7lO7GsGZq2G4IlT' >"$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf"
output=$(omarchy-install-chromium-google-account 2>&1) ||
  fail "installer handles a flags file that holds only the workaround" "exit $?: $output"
grep -qE -- '^--oauth2-client-(id|secret)=' "$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf" &&
  fail "installer strips a flags file that holds only the workaround" "$(cat "$HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf")"
grep -qxF 'stub-install-browser chrome' "$HOME/actions.log" 2>/dev/null ||
  fail "installer still installs Chrome after stripping an OAuth-only flags file"
pass "installer handles a flags file that holds only the workaround"
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (exit 1):

```text
ok - installer removes oauth2 workaround flags and installs Chrome when missing
ok - installer skips Chrome when it is already present
exit 1: Chromium Google account support...
not ok - installer handles a flags file that holds only the workaround
```

With the suggested `sed -i --follow-symlinks` change in both files and both blocks appended (exit 0):

```text
ok - installer removes oauth2 workaround flags and installs Chrome when missing
ok - installer skips Chrome when it is already present
ok - migration strips a flags file that holds only the workaround
ok - installer handles a flags file that holds only the workaround
```

A smaller alternative that keeps `mktemp`/`mv`, not run: `grep -vE -- '...' "$file" >"$tmp" || (( $? == 1 ))`. Avoid `|| true`, which would also hide grep's exit 2 (read error) and then `mv` a partial file over the original.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Knock-on effects (source reading, not run end to end):** `bin/omarchy-update` calls `omarchy-migrate` under `set -e`, so the rest of the update is skipped each time; `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro` reports "Omarchy migrations did not complete. Fix the error above..." with no error above it. `omarchy-migrate` itself was run: it exited 1 on two successive runs and a later migration never ran.

**Premise wording.** Reports on #2225 and #8394 tie the OAuth flags to a browser-process SIGTRAP on Chromium 151.0.7922.137 and .173 (Google Search, sign-in, Gmail), and one partial A/B test on #8394 supports it. No report found names Chromium 136 or Sync. Other Omarchy Chromium SIGTRAPs have other explanations: a GPU-process failure with the shipped default flags file (no OAuth lines, #8394), and a crash fixed by replacing the profile, where the flag state is not stated (#2225). Suggested: say "Chromium 151 and later" and drop "136+" and "enabling Sync" in the installer, migration, commit and PR text; soften the manual to "has been reported to make Chromium crash"; consider referencing the open #8394, since #2225 has been closed since 2025-10-05.

**Pattern mismatch.** The installer and migration strip only lines starting with `--oauth2-client-`, but the menu's `disabled` check is unanchored. An indented line is still passed to Chromium by the launcher and is not stripped; a commented line is ignored by Chromium but keeps the row selectable. Both only affect hand-edited files. Suggested: use one anchored, whitespace-tolerant pattern such as `^[[:space:]]*--oauth2-client-(id|secret)=` in the installer, the migration and the menu's `disabled` check. In the installer and migration it fixed the reproduced indented case.

**Symlinks and mode.** `mv` replaces a symlinked `chromium-flags.conf` with a plain file (the dotfiles copy keeps both OAuth lines) and changes the mode from 0644 to 0600. The `sed -i --follow-symlinks` change keeps the link and mode.

**Related open PRs.**
- #12244 rewrites `bin/omarchy-install-chromium-google-account` in the opposite direction (keeps the OAuth flags, with overrideable credentials) and conflicts textually.
- #13189, #13762, #13481 and #10884 conflict in `bin/omarchy-refresh-chromium`; #13189 also uses the `CONFIG_FILE` variable this PR deletes.
- #10446 rewrites the same menu row's `when` to `omarchy-cmd-present chromium` and asserts it in `menu-test.sh`.

**Verified:**
- With default flags plus the OAuth lines, the migration and installer remove only the two OAuth lines.
- `omarchy refresh chromium` no longer re-adds them (source reading: it only restores the shipped default file).
- `omarchy-pkg-present google-chrome` checks the same package that `omarchy-install-browser chrome` installs.
- Both stated tests pass at the head and merged into the base tip, and fail against the merge-base code.
- The PR merges cleanly into the current base tip.

**Optional test improvement:** the new test never runs `migrations/1789450436.sh`, and both of its fixtures contain other flags, so the OAuth-only case is never exercised. It also ignores the installer's exit status (the harness runs each file with plain `bash`). The reproducer blocks above cover both.
</details>
